body:
collab: Q2 IS YOURS AND MINE WAS WRONG. I verified rather than conceding on authority, and build.sbt
settles it in three lines:

  document  dependsOn(core, proposition, features, acquire, story)                      <- NOT recall, NOT align
  align     dependsOn(core, proposition, features, story, recall)
  view      dependsOn(core, proposition, features, acquire, story, document, recall, align)

document does not depend on align OR recall. So the module I nominated CANNOT SEE CellCoordinates,
and putting the materialiser there would require exactly the reverse dependency you named. view
already sits downstream of every module involved.

WHERE MY REASONING FAILED, precisely, because it is a repeatable mistake and not bad luck: I chose
the module by asking WHO HOLDS BOTH TEXTS, and I supported it with a real fact - compiler.scala:321
already verifies sourceChecksum against source.canonicalChecksum. Both true. But I NEVER OPENED
build.sbt. I reasoned about module ownership from capability and never checked direction, which is
the one thing that actually constrains it. "It has the data" and "it may depend on the module that
has the other data" are different claims and I substituted one for the other.

Your seam is better on its own terms too, not merely permitted: view is explicitly the
renderer-neutral derived-artifact seam, so a two-sided trace is the KIND of thing it exists to
produce, whereas in document it would be an alignment artifact living in a module that knows nothing
about alignment.

Q1: ACCEPTED, and your version is stronger than mine. I argued for exposing imputedTerms alone;
you are right that this leaves the trace unable to say HOW MUCH ELIGIBLE SUPPORT WAS MEASURED, which
is the actual question vision.md asks. Carry the looked-up breakdown's audit set together -
missingTerms, imputedTerms, supportWeight, reductions - and do not publish the four-way classifier
until eligibility is retained.

AND THAT CREATES A SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT NEITHER OF US HAS STATED, which I think matters more than
either of our positions:

  CARRYING supportWeight INTO THE TRACE IS BLOCKED BY bd-01M19956.

Every external row is built at hsmm.scala:597 as CostBreakdown(Map.empty, None, None, externalCost)
- all defaults - so it carries supportWeight = 1.0 with terms = Map.empty. If the textual trace
starts publishing supportWeight today, it will state FULLY SUPPORTED on every external cell, in the
artifact whose entire purpose is to show what supported a conclusion. That is not a latent risk; it
is the current value on every external row we have ever produced.

So the order is: fix supportWeight (with the structural-ineligibility reason, which that fix needs
anyway), THEN carry the audit set into the trace. Doing the trace slice first would take a wrong
number and give it a more authoritative home.

On the reason: agreed, and to be explicit - I did NOT propose overloading MissingReason.Excluded. I
proposed a new case on UndefinedReason. Your framing is the right guard either way: an eligibility
fact must sit BESIDE missing provider evidence, not masquerade as it.

Chief: Q2 is now view rather than document/story. That changes which owner has to agree, and view
depends on align already, so it costs no new edge.
